newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Regional index boosts Singapore shares at close.
newsitem.headline: Regional index boosts Singapore shares at close.

text.p: Buying interest in components of the recently launched Business-Times Singapore Regional Index (BT-SRI) kept Singapore shares active on Friday, dealers said.
Good trading volumes were also seen in Malaysian over the counter stocks on the back of the Kuala Lumpur Composite Index making a strong push through the 1,200 level.
Dealers said they expected "more of the same" for Singapore shares next week but were uncertain if Malaysian OTCs could sustain their run.
The Straits Times Industrials Index closed at 2,194.75, down 2.94 points. The BT-SRI surged 12.55 points to 1,084.83.
"We're seeing a lot of orders from Europe, especially the UK," said a dealer.
Among the BT-SRI components that closed strongly were the Jardine group of companies, foreign tranches of banks like UOB and DBS, and Total Access Communication.
Hongkong Land, part of Jardine, led actives with 17.53 million shares and rose US$0.08 to US$2.86.

The market was eyeing the debut of interior design and furniture firm Nobel Design Holdings on the second board on Monday, dealers said. Nobel's initital public offer was 124.75 times subscribed, the highest this year.-Josephine Ng 65-8703094
